```sql
-- name: top_products
-- owner: merchandising
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
WITH ord AS (
    SELECT o.id
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
line_v AS (
    SELECT ol.order_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents,
           ol.variant_id::uuid AS variant_id
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN ord ON ord.id = ol.order_id
),
prod AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           lv.order_id,
           lv.variant_id,
           lv.quantity,
           lv.line_total_cents
      FROM line_v lv
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = lv.variant_id
),
agg AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(DISTINCT order_id)     AS order_count,
           sum(quantity)                AS quantity,
           sum(line_total_cents)        AS revenue_cents,
           count(DISTINCT variant_id)   AS variant_count
      FROM prod
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       a.order_count,
       a.quantity,
       a.revenue_cents,
       a.variant_count
  FROM agg a
  JOIN products p ON p.id = a.product_id
 ORDER BY a.quantity DESC, a.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De orderfilter wordt eerst apart toegepast, zodat de aggregatie niet op de volledige join met `orders` hoeft te draaien en de dure externe sort op `(p.id, o.id)` verdwijnt. Het joinen met `products` gebeurt pas na de aggregatie, op één rij per product. Tie-breaking in de ORDER BY is gelijk aan het origineel, dus de volgorde bij gelijke waarden blijft even willekeurig als voorheen.
